$comment: Machine-readable headline numbers of the paired-oracle study, transcribed from REPORT_PAIRED_ORACLE.md / REPORT_BF16_ORACLE.md (study run 2026-09-21). Raw per-candidate calibration JSONs were not committed and the local oracle cache has since been deleted; re-run the commands in the report's Reproduction section to regenerate raw evidence. Weights and dataset text are never committed. Do not edit numbers here without re-deriving them.

study.host: Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB unified memory

bf16_oracle.verdict: Mapping, attention/GDN reordering, norms, MTP handling and config emission are proven correct at BF16 on two architectures; every subsequent difference is attributable to quantization.

quantizer_equivalence.verdict: Our BF16-GGUF->3-bit quantization path is numerically equivalent to mlx-lm's (same error profile to 4+ significant digits); requantizing Q3_K_M to MLX 3-bit adds 6-13.5% per-module error on top of the 3-bit ceiling.

level1_calibration.size_unit_note: size_mib values are the report's 'M' column (MiB, approximate)
findings: The 3-bit affine cliff (~+1.0 nat/token, ~2.8x perplexity) dominates and appears with or without double quantization; double quantization is behaviorally secondary (+0.03 nats) although it adds 6-13.5% per-module error.
Every 3-bit-containing profile is Pareto-dominated by plain 4-bit, including mixed_3_6 which spends more bytes and is still 3.2x worse in KL.

qat_control.verdict: The QAT pair is the same weights in different formats; fidelity at low bits comes from aligning weights to the target grid (QAT), not from smarter PTQ.

llama_cpp.note: Homebrew llama.cpp on the study host (`llama-quantize --version`, re-checked 2026-09-22). The original Q3_K_M derivation log did not record the build; pin the build when re-deriving, this is a known reproducibility gap now documented in the report's Reproduction section.
